Traupman 132, 136

bellus, bella, bellum

adjective

nice, lovely, fine

(vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Catull.; Cic. in epistulīs)

The everyday word for anything nice: a place, a day, a present. The adverb bellē is “nicely, fine”.

Other words

  • jūcundus, jūcunda, jūcundum — pleasant, delightful

    adjective · also used · classical · Caes. BC 1.86: pergrātum et jūcundum (Lewis & Short)

  • lepidus, lepida, lepidum — charming, delightful

    adjective · also used · classical · Ter. And. 5.4.45: ō lepidum patrem! (Lewis & Short); Traupman 156

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; in Cicerōne rāra)

  • suāvis, suāve — sweet, pleasant (to the senses)

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.3.23: odor suāvis et jūcundus (Lewis & Short)

  • jūcunditās, jūcunditātis f. — pleasantness, delight

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 1.59 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 156

  • concinnus, concinna, concinnum — neat, pleasing; courteous

    also used · classical · Traupman 156

    Properly “neatly put together”.

Examples

  • illum puerīs locum esse bellissimum dūximus

    we thought it the nicest place for the boysCic. Att. 5.17.3

  • Prōrsus, est diēs bellus et tepidus.

    All in all, it’s a nice warm day.Traupman 132

  • Nōn bellē fēcistī quī id dīxerīs.

    It wasn’t nice of you to say that.Traupman 104

See also kind, pretty, cute.
